Okey Anyiam

Democratic candidate for Court of Criminal Appeals, Place 3, Texas

Criminal defense attorney (Dallas)

Okey Anyiam is a Dallas criminal defense attorney who has been licensed to practice law in Texas since 1997. He won the Democratic primary for Texas Court of Criminal Appeals, Place 3 on March 3, 2026, where he was the only candidate. In the November 3, 2026 general election he faces Republican Thomas Smith and Libertarian Mark Ash for the open seat.

Where Anyiam stands

Judicial independence
Says he will not yield to outside influence or intimidation from anyone, including another branch of government, and will not let re-election concerns affect his rulings.
Judicial philosophy
Supports upholding the law and following its clear legislative intent without legislating from the bench, and supports equal access to justice for all.
Court caseload and docket
Proposes working with the other judges to make changes so the court can hear more cases than it does now.
Guidance on unappealed issues
Proposes giving guidance on important issues that appear in the record but were not raised on appeal, so similar issues don't wait years for an opinion in later appeals.
Partisan balance on the court
Argues that the court should not have only Republican judges and that electing a Democrat would bring balance to the court.
Due process
Says his goal over 28 years of criminal practice has been to make sure defendants' due process rights are upheld and justice is served.

Background

  • Criminal defense attorney in Dallas, Texas
  • Licensed to practice law in Texas since 1997
  • About 28 years of criminal law practice; says he has handled several thousand criminal cases
  • Democratic nominee, Texas Court of Criminal Appeals Place 3 (won the March 3, 2026 primary)
